1.title: The Processes: Starting Up, Directing and Initiating a Project
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: The Processes: Starting Up, Directing and Initiating a Project. It covers the exam area The prince two processes. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Explain the purpose, objectives and context of the processes starting up a project, directing a project and initiating a project. Explain where the seven processes fit across the project life. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two processes (fifteen percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: The seven processes
1.text: The seven processes. The processes take the project from start to close. There are seven. one. Process: Starting up a project. Short idea: Is there a viable and worthwhile project? two. Process: Directing a project. Short idea: The board decides, runs throughout. three. Process: Initiating a project. Short idea: Build solid foundations. four. Process: Controlling a stage. Short idea: Day-to-day control of a stage. five. Process: Managing product delivery. Short idea: Link between project manager and team manager. six. Process: Managing a stage boundary. Short idea: Close one stage and plan the next. seven. Process: Closing a project. Short idea: Confirm acceptance and wrap up.

1.title: The seven processes, continued
1.text: The seven processes. The figure shows this: The seven processes along the project life: pre-project, initiation stage, delivery stages, final stage.

1.title: Starting up a project
1.text: Starting up a project. Purpose: ensure the prerequisites for initiation are in place by answering: do we have a viable and worthwhile project? Objectives include: the project has a justified reason, the project management team and approach are chosen, and everyone knows what is needed to initiate the project. Context: it happens before the project proper (the pre-project period). Main outputs: the project brief and the initiation stage plan.

1.title: Directing a project
1.text: Directing a project. Purpose: enable the project board to be accountable for the project's success by making key decisions and exercising overall control, while delegating day-to-day management to the project manager. Objectives include: authority for the project is in place, the board has control at every decision point, and management is supported with ad hoc direction. Context: it runs from start-up to closure. Key board decisions: authorize initiation, authorize the project, authorize each stage or exception plan, give ad hoc direction, authorize project closure. Exam tip: Directing is the board's process and spans the whole project. The project manager does not direct; the board does.

1.title: Initiating a project
1.text: Initiating a project. Purpose: establish solid foundations so the organization understands the work needed to deliver the project's products before committing to significant spend. Objectives include: everyone agrees what the project must achieve, why, how, by whom, and at what cost, quality and risk, and baselines are set. Context: it happens in the initiation stage. Main output: the project initiation documentation (P I D): the business case, the approaches, the team structure, the project plan and how the project is tailored. Exam tip: Starting up produces the project brief; initiating produces the P I D. Do not swap them. Exam tip: The board decides at every gate: it authorizes initiation, the project, each stage and closure.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which process answers the question "do we have a viable and worthwhile project?". The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Starting up a project. Starting up checks the prerequisites for initiation.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which statements about directing a project are C O R R E C T? (one) It enables the project board to be accountable. (two) It runs from start-up to closure. (three) It is carried out by the project manager. (four) It happens only at the end. The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: one and two. Directing is the board's process and spans the project.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Identify the missing word. The blank is produced during initiating a project and baselines the project's plans and approaches. The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: P I D. The project initiation documentation is the main output.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. At which point does the board decide to authorize the project? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: After initiating a project. The board authorizes the project after the P I D has been prepared.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which process produces the project brief and the initiation stage plan? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Starting up a project. Those are outputs of starting up.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which process establishes solid foundations before significant spend is committed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Initiating a project. Initiating sets the foundations.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many processes does prince two seven have? Answer: Seven. Question two. What question does starting up a project answer? Answer: Do we have a viable and worthwhile project? Question three. Who carries out directing a project? Answer: The project board.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the main output of initiating a project? Answer: The project initiation documentation (P I D). Question five. What are the outputs of starting up? Answer: The project brief and the initiation stage plan. Question six. When does directing a project happen? Answer: Throughout, from start-up to closure.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Process: Purpose in a phrase. Starting up: viable and worthwhile? (project brief). Directing: board decisions and control, throughout.
